key_insight: Telescopic Language Models train one Transformer to behave like a whole family of models with different compute budgets. Instead of separate models or compression runs, a single nested-capacity model can serve multiple budgets from one artifact.
problem_solved: Deploying language models across many compute budgets usually requires training or compressing separate models for each point on the efficiency-performance tradeoff curve. This paper addresses the need for a single model that can adapt smoothly to different inference budgets.
method: Train a nested-capacity Transformer called a Telescopic Language Model (TLM), where smaller prefixes of the model act as lower-capacity submodels.
Use stochastic prefix supervision: at each step, train one randomly truncated prefix of the capacity axis against the full next-token target.
Include a full-capacity anchor pass so the largest model remains well-trained while all smaller prefixes learn to perform as valid language models.
impact: For practitioners, this offers a more flexible deployment strategy: one trained model can support multiple latency, cost, and quality targets without retraining from scratch. It simplifies serving and can reduce engineering overhead for multi-budget inference.
